name: Anohni
label: Secretly Canadian
lede: She started in the after-hours bars of 1992, renamed her band after a woman she met days before that woman died, and won the Mercury Prize with a record that jumped 119 places on the UK chart in a week.

eras.title: From San Jose to the Lower East Side
eras.text: Born in England, raised in Amsterdam and the Bay Area, Anohni landed in Manhattan at 19 and built a stage out of after-hours bars and late-night theatre. The name the band would later carry came from a woman Anohni met once, days before her death.

years.h: Born in Chichester, England
years.p: Anohni's family moves to Amsterdam in 1977 and to the San Francisco Bay Area in 1981, settling in San Jose. She has said she saw her own reflection in Culture Club's Boy George.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Anohni attended Lincoln High School in San Jose, studied music and was an avid record collector: OMD, Kate Bush, Culture Club, Alison Moyet and Marc and the Mambas are the names it lists.

Wikipedia says she recalled seeing "her reflection" in [[Boy George|2787bddf-6439-4c73-8162-5f4a1e5fa030]], who would sing on the second Johnsons album more than two decades later.

years.h: Anohni moves to Manhattan for NYU's Experimental Theater Wing
years.p: She spends the early 1990s singing in after-hours bars and clubs over pre-recorded cassettes, and writing and directing late-night theatre.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: ANOHNI Turns Toward Hope · Wikipedia: Anohni
years.h: Blacklips Performance Cult starts, with Johanna Constantine
years.p: The collective is a queer and trans cabaret-theatre that gets its start in New York. A March 2023 compilation, Blacklips Bar: Androgyns and Deviants, collects its 1992-1995 work.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily describes the compilation as documenting the group's work on AIDS and environmental decline.

Wikipedia dates the founding of Blacklips (originally just Blacklips) to 1992, with Anohni and Johanna Constantine as co-founders.

years.cap: Antony and the Johnsons at theTeatro Real, Madrid, Spain. · Wikimedia
years.src: The FADER: ANOHNI is building tiny fires in a world made of darkness · Wikipedia: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross
years.h: Anohni meets Marsha P. Johnson at Pride, days before her death
years.p: Anohni told The FADER she kissed Johnson's hand and thanked her at Gay Pride in 1992. Johnson died days later, and "the Johnsons" honors her.
years.xp:
The FADER reports that Anohni calls the name "sacred ancestry" and describes Johnson, the gay-liberation activist, as "Jesus as a girl" for her work on liberation.

Thirty years on, Alvin Baltrop's photograph of Johnson is the cover of My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross.

years.h: The Birth of Anne Frank / The Ascension of Marsha P. Johnson
years.p: A New York Foundation for the Arts grant funds the piece. Anohni then asks musicians to help record songs written in the early 1990s.

eras.title: The Johnsons find a stage
eras.text: A chamber band forms around a voice people compare to Nina Simone. Their first records come out on an indie label run by a man from the world of Current 93.

years.cap: Teatro de la Ciudad de México. Festival de la Ciudad de México · Wikimedia
years.h: First concert as Antony and the Johnsons, inside a William Basinski installation
years.p: The ensemble plays The Kitchen in 1997 as part of Basinski's installation Life on Mars. Cellist [[Julia Kent|63733317-8113-413a-8b8b-7ef89cd1f50d]] and violinist [[Maxim Moston|ca7ff952-74b6-4379-bfbb-03c86e1720c9]] are listed as members from 1999.

years.h: Debut album on David Tibet's Durtro label
years.p: The self-titled first record arrives in 2000, followed in 2001 by the EP I Fell in Love with a Dead Boy, which includes covers of Angelo Badalamenti and Current 93 songs.

years.h: Anohni sings backup for [[Lou Reed|9d1ebcfe-4c15-4d18-95d3-d919898638a1]] on the Animal Serenade tour
years.p: She sings on songs from Reed's The Raven. A few years on she is in his Berlin band too, a friendship that shows up on the 2023 album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Anohni joined Reed as a supporting vocalist from 2003. She sang backup, with Sharon Jones and a children's choir, in his first complete performance of Berlin at St Ann's Warehouse in December 2006, and again at the State Theatre in Sydney in January 2007.

eras.title: A bird, a prize, a lot of guests
eras.text: I Am a Bird Now turns an indie chamber-pop record into a national event. Everyone from Lou Reed to Björk wants her on their records.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Am a Bird Now
years.h: I Am a Bird Now: Lou Reed, Boy George, Rufus Wainwright, Devendra Banhart
years.p: Secretly Canadian releases it in North America and Rough Trade in Europe. The cover is Peter Hujar's photograph of Candy Darling on her deathbed.
years.xp:
Reed plays guitar and sings on "Fistful of Love" and Boy George appears on "You Are My Sister", according to Wikipedia. Rufus Wainwright and Devendra Banhart are also on it.

The Guardian later ranked it 40th on its list of the 100 best albums of the 21st century, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Antony Hegarty from Antony and the Johnsons. Doing a clap song. Hace unos días Elena lo describió acertadamente como "algo así como un Robert Smith autista". · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: I Am a Bird Now · Wikipedia: Anohni
years.h: Antony and the Johnsons win the Mercury Prize
years.p: The album jumps from No. 135 to No. 16 on the UK chart the week after, which Wikipedia calls the biggest jump in the history of the prize.
years.xp:
Mojo also named it Album of the Year, per Wikipedia. Its song "Bird Gerhl" ended up on the soundtrack of V for Vendetta.

Wikipedia puts UK sales at 220,000 by September 2011.

years.h: Turning: live video portraits of New York's underground women
years.p: With filmmaker Charles Atlas, the band tours the piece to Rome, London, Paris, Madrid and Braga. The Guardian gave it five stars.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes the Guardian calling it "fragile, life affirming, and truly wonderful", and Le Monde headlining it a "Concert-manifeste transsexuel".

years.h: Sessions with [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]] in Jamaica and Iceland
years.p: Two songs, "The Dull Flame of Desire" and "My Juvenile", land on her 2007 album Volta. Anohni duets with her in London, Reykjavik and New York.

years.h: Anohni sings "Blind" on [[Hercules and Love Affair|b62ecfe7-b2e6-4d40-b7d2-8f12d3f51ed6]]'s debut
years.p: She appears on five tracks of the disco record, and "Blind" is the one people remember. Entertainment Weekly ranked it No. 2 on its 10 Best Singles of 2008.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Pitchfork voted "Blind" the best track of 2008. Anohni would return to Hercules and Love Affair in June 2022 on In Amber, leading six tracks and co-writing them with Budgie, the drummer of Siouxsie and the Banshees.

years.h: Another World EP: five songs
years.p: It is a bridge between I Am a Bird Now and the environmental turn of the next record.

eras.title: Landscape and the future
eras.text: The subject widens from the self to the planet, and the stage widens to orchestras. The band plays symphony halls, fashion houses and a curated festival.

years.h: The Crying Light: arrangements by Nico Muhly
years.p: Mixed by Bryce Goggin, it tops European charts, Wikipedia says. Anohni calls it a record about landscape and the future.
years.xp: Ann Powers of the LA Times called it "the most personal environmentalist statement possible" and, as music, "simply exquisite", Wikipedia reports.

years.h: Symphony halls with the Manchester Camerata and others
years.p: The Manchester International Festival staging uses lasers by Chris Levine. Summer dates follow with the Opera Orchestra of Lyon, Metropole Orchestra and Montreux Jazz Festival Orchestra.

years.h: Swanlights, plus a book of Anohni's drawings and collages
years.p: Abrams publishes the book edition with photography by Don Felix Cervantes. Anohni plays Lincoln Center that month for the late dancer Kazuo Ohno.

years.h: Cut the World: live with the Danish Radio Orchestra
years.p: The album includes a spoken piece, "Future Feminism". The video, directed by Nabil Elderkin, has Willem Dafoe, Carice van Houten and Marina Abramović.

years.h: Anohni curates Meltdown at the Southbank Centre

eras.title: Anohni, unveiled
eras.text: A last show with Lou Reed, then a name change, a hard electronic record and an Oscar nomination she never got to sing at.

years.h: Final Lou Reed show, at Salle Pleyel in Paris
years.p: Anohni and the Johnsons play with Reed there, his last performance before his death.
years.xp: Anohni told interviewers that the conversations with Reed before he died shaped "Sliver of Ice" on the 2023 album. Wikipedia quotes her on the moments that were changing how he saw things: "He was a hardcore kind of guy."

years.h: Anohni announces Hopelessness, the first record under that name
years.p: She had used the name personally for years. It is co-produced with Oneohtrix Point Never and Hudson Mohawke.

years.h: Hopelessness: drones, surveillance, capital punishment
years.p: An electronic record with, per Wikipedia, some sharp teeth. "Drone Bomb Me" arrives with a Nabil Elderkin video starring Naomi Campbell.
years.xp:
Hudson Mohawke says Anohni worked hands-on in Pro Tools, arranging and editing. It was nominated for the 2016 Mercury Prize, and she was nominated for a Brit Award, both per Wikipedia. Metacritic gives it 83.

The New York Times called the tour, where she performed with her face under a veil in front of lip-syncing women, punk and radical empathy.

years.big: First openly trans performer nominated for an Academy Award
years.h: "Manta Ray" is nominated for an Oscar; Anohni is not invited to sing
years.p: Wikipedia says the Academy described her as cut from the show for time constraints, though she says she was never asked to perform. She stayed home.
years.xp: Anohni wrote that singing about ecocide "might not sell advertising space", per Wikipedia, and pointed to systems that give trans people diminished opportunities. "Manta Ray" was written with J. Ralph for the film Racing Extinction.

years.h: Paradise EP, with a last track for anyone who emails Anohni a sentence
years.p: Same producers as Hopelessness. The final track goes to people who send in a sentence or two about what they care about most.

eras.title: The Johnsons come back
eras.text: Anohni returns to the band name and to a warmer sound, with a new producer and ten years of unreleased writing. The New Yorker calls it its No. 1 album of the year.

years.cap: Antony Hegarty (with Sissy Nobby) at Donaufestival, Krems, Austria · Wikimedia
years.h: Blacklips Bar: Androgyns and Deviants compiles the 1992-1995 work
years.p: The March 2023 compilation documents her performance collective's years in New York.

years.h: Anohni and the Johnsons return with "It Must Change"
years.p: The Times says she seems to sing in the voice of Mother Earth. The video stars Munroe Bergdorf, and the single is the first from Jimmy Hogarth's new studio band.

q: Hopelessness is the most strategic record I've ever made.
years.src: Wikipedia: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross · Album of the Year: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross · The FADER: ANOHNI is building tiny fires in a world made of darkness · Bandcamp Daily: ANOHNI Turns Toward Hope
years.h: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross on Secretly Canadian
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and ranked it No. 9 of 2023. Jimmy Hogarth co-produces; the cover is Alvin Baltrop's photograph of Marsha P. Johnson.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Hogarth and Anohni started in 2022 and recorded three or four songs a day over two weeks, with many vocals Anohni's first takes. The reference points were Nina Simone and Jimmy Scott. Metacritic gives it 88 from 17 reviews; Album of the Year lists Pitchfork at 87, which is its 8.7.

The FADER says Rough Trade recommended Hogarth, whose credits include Amy Winehouse and Tina Turner (per Bandcamp Daily), and that the songs draw on ten years of unreleased writing. Anohni told the FADER that Hopelessness "is the most strategic record I've ever made."
play: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross

years.src: Treble: Watch the new ANOHNI video for Why Am I Alive Now?
years.h: Hunter Schafer directs the video for "Why Am I Alive Now?"
years.p: Shot at an industrial complex above the Pacific. Schafer says she wanted to focus on finding sisterhood in a world that does nothing to help.
years.xp: The video came out two days before the album. A live playback on the Rebismusic YouTube channel on July 6 featured Anohni, a Q&A with Schafer and Nomi Ruiz.

years.h: The New Yorker names it album of the year
years.p: The New York Times puts it at No. 10, Mondo Sonoro at No. 5, and Pitchfork at No. 9.
